Imagine… every piece of iron on Earth suddenly vanished.
What would happen to you?
You are driving across a bridge.
The radio is on.
Nothing feels wrong.
Then.
Your car falls apart around you.
Steel is about ninety-eight percent iron.
The bridge has nothing left to hold it up.
Skyscrapers lose every steel beam.
But you won't see it.
The iron in your blood is gone too.
Your blood can't carry oxygen.
You black out in about ten seconds.
Deep below, the iron core disappears.
Earth loses a third of its mass.
And the magnetic field that shields us… shuts off.
Here's the twist.
That iron was never really from Earth.
It was forged in exploding stars, long before our planet existed.
So remember.
Your blood holds about four grams of star metal… enough for one small nail.
